## Requirements

- Node.js >= 18
- Yarn 1.x (classic)
- *(LVGL conversion only)* Rust toolchain + [wasm-pack](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/)

## Install

This is a private package hosted on [GitHub Packages](https://github.com/worklouder/wl-device-kit/packages). Authenticate with a GitHub personal access token that has `read:packages` scope:

```bash
# .npmrc (project or user level)
@worklouder:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${GITHUB_TOKEN}
```

```bash
yarn add @worklouder/wl-device-kit
```

> **Electron / browser renderer:** For contexts that only need shared enums and types, import from the `browser_safe` subpath to avoid pulling in Node-only transports:
> ```ts
> import { DeviceType, DeviceLayoutType } from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit/browser_safe";
> ```

## Build

```bash
yarn install
yarn build        # compile TypeScript → dist/
yarn wasm-build   # compile Rust → WASM (requires Rust + wasm-pack)
yarn build:all    # wasm-build + build in one step
```

## Quick start

```ts
import {
  WLDeviceDiscovery,
  WLDeviceCommImpl,
  WLRPCApi,
  ConnectionEventType,
} from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit";

// 1. Discover devices
const discovery = new WLDeviceDiscovery();
const devices = discovery.findWLDevices();

if (devices.length === 0) {
  console.log("No devices found");
  process.exit(1);
}

// 2. Connect
const comm = new WLDeviceCommImpl();

comm.onConnectionEvent((event) => {
  if (event.type === ConnectionEventType.DISCONNECTED) {
    console.log("Device disconnected");
  }
});

await comm.connect(devices[0]);

// 3. Use the high-level API
const api = new WLRPCApi(comm);
const status = await api.getDeviceStatus();
console.log("Firmware:", status.firmwareVersion);
console.log("Battery:", status.batteryPercentage, "%");

// 4. Disconnect when done
await comm.disconnect();
```

## Architecture

```
src/
├── common/types/          # Shared enums and interfaces (DeviceType, ConnectionType, WLDevice, JSON-RPC types)
├── utils/                 # EventEmitter, string escaping helpers
├── wl_permissions/        # OS-level device permission checks
├── wl_device_discovery/   # USB HID + serial port scanning
├── wl_device_comm/        # Low-level transport layer (HID & serial framing, request queue)
├── wl_rpc_client/         # JSON-RPC 2.0 request/response serialization
├── wl_rpc_api/            # High-level typed API (system, filesystem, lighting, media, UI)
├── wl_release/            # Firmware & app release checking via GitHub Releases API
├── wl_lvgl/               # LVGL image conversion (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, TIFF, WebP, ICO, TGA, … ↔ LVGL binary via WASM)
└── wl_device_programmer/  # ESP32 firmware flashing via serial (esptool-js)
```

| Module | Entry point | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Permissions** | `WLPermissions` | Check OS-level access to HID devices (macOS Input Monitoring, Linux device nodes) |
| **Device Discovery** | `WLDeviceDiscovery` | Scan USB for connected Work Louder devices and bootloaders |
| **Device Comm** | `WLDeviceCommImpl` | Open a transport connection (HID or serial), manage the send queue |
| **RPC Client** | `WLRPCClient` | Serialize JSON-RPC 2.0 requests, manage call IDs, parse responses |
| **RPC API** | `WLRPCApi` | High-level typed methods for every firmware capability |
| **Release** | `WLRelease` | Check for firmware and app updates via GitHub Releases API with ETag caching |
| **LVGL Converter** | `convertImageToLvgl` / `convertLvglToImage` | Convert images (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, TIFF, WebP, ICO, TGA, and more) to/from LVGL v9 binary format via a Rust/WASM bridge |
| **Device Programmer** | `WLDeviceProgrammer` | Flash firmware to ESP32-based devices over serial (bootloader mode) |

## Device discovery

```ts
import { WLDeviceDiscovery, DeviceType } from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit";

const discovery = new WLDeviceDiscovery();

const all = discovery.findWLDevices();                         // all Work Louder HID devices
const knobs = discovery.findWLDevices([DeviceType.Knob]);      // filter by product type
const bootloaders = await discovery.findWLBootloaderDevices(); // DFU devices on serial ports
```

## Permissions

Before opening a device, verify that the process has OS-level access. `WLPermissions` abstracts platform differences:

| Platform | What is checked | Required dependency |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **macOS** | Input Monitoring authorization | `node-mac-permissions` (optional peer, macOS only) |
| **Linux** | Read/write access to `/dev/hidraw*` nodes | None (uses Node built-ins) |
| **Windows** | Always returns `true` | None |

```ts
import { WLDeviceDiscovery, WLPermissions } from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit";

const discovery = new WLDeviceDiscovery();
const permissions = new WLPermissions();

const devices = discovery.findWLDevices();
const allowed = await permissions.check(devices.map((d) => d.portPath));

if (!allowed) {
  // macOS: enable Input Monitoring in System Settings → Privacy & Security
  // Linux: check udev rules or run with the appropriate group membership
  console.error("Insufficient permissions to access HID devices");
  process.exit(1);
}
```

> **Linux note:** `check()` returns `true` when no device paths are supplied. A check run before any device is plugged in will succeed — call it again after discovery returns results.

## Connection events

Subscribe to transport lifecycle changes on the `WLDeviceComm` instance:

```ts
const unsub = comm.onConnectionEvent((event) => {
  switch (event.type) {
    case ConnectionEventType.CONNECTED:
      console.log("Connected");
      break;
    case ConnectionEventType.DISCONNECTED:
      console.log("Disconnected");
      break;
    case ConnectionEventType.ERROR:
      console.error("Error:", event.error);
      break;
  }
});

unsub(); // stop listening
```

## Device notifications

Devices can push unsolicited JSON-RPC notifications (no `id`, just a `method`). Register handlers on the comm layer:

```ts
comm.addNotifyHandler("kb.radial", (params) => {
  console.log("Radial menu event:", params);
});

comm.removeNotifyHandler("kb.radial"); // remove when no longer needed
```

## Lighting

`WLDeviceLightingConfig` has two zones — `backlight` and `underglow` — each a `SideLightingConfig`:

```ts
import { LightingEffect } from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit";
import type { WLDeviceLightingConfig } from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit";

const config: WLDeviceLightingConfig = {
  backlight: {
    effect: LightingEffect.solid,
    brightness: 0.8,
    color: 0xFF5500, // packed RGB integer
  },
  underglow: {
    effect: LightingEffect.rainbow,
    speed: 0.5,
    brightness: 1.0,
  },
};

await api.sendLightingPreview(config);
```

> `color` is a **packed RGB integer** (e.g. `0xFF0000` for red), not a hex string. `brightness`, `speed`, and `magic` are **normalized 0–1**.

## LVGL image conversion

Convert images to LVGL v9 binary format and back. The input format is auto-detected; PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, TIFF, WebP, ICO, TGA, and other formats supported by the Rust `image` crate are all accepted. Conversion runs in a Rust/WASM module (`icu_lib`) that loads lazily on first use.

```ts
import { convertImageToLvgl, convertLvglToImage } from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit";
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

const png = new Uint8Array(readFileSync("wallpaper.png"));
const lvgl = convertImageToLvgl(png);
writeFileSync("wallpaper.bin", lvgl);

const roundTrip = convertLvglToImage(lvgl);
writeFileSync("roundtrip.png", roundTrip);
```

> The encoder uses **indexed 8-bit color (I8)** and LVGL v9 format. Conversion is lossy for most images due to color quantization. A second encode/decode pass is idempotent within a small per-channel delta.

## Release checks

`WLRelease` queries the GitHub Releases API to check for firmware and application updates. It supports ETag-based conditional requests to minimise API usage and provides an in-memory cache with a 60-second TTL.

```ts
import { WLRelease, DeviceType } from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit";
import type { ReleaseInfo } from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit";

const release = new WLRelease(logger);
```

### Check for latest firmware release

```ts
import { RepositoryType } from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit/wl_release";

const latest = await release.getLatestRelease(RepositoryType.NomadFirmware);
if (latest) {
  console.log("Latest version:", latest.version);
  console.log("Download:", latest.downloadUrl);
}
```

### Check for latest app release (including pre-release)

```ts
const beta = await release.getLatestRelease(RepositoryType.InputApp, true);
```

### Determine if a firmware update should be applied

`shouldUpdateFirmware` orchestrates the full check: it verifies the app is up-to-date before recommending a firmware update. Beta app users are always checked against pre-release firmware. Returns the `ReleaseInfo` for the available update, or `undefined` when no update is needed.

```ts
const update = await release.shouldUpdateFirmware(
  "1.2.0",   // current app version
  "0.9.1",   // firmware version from device
  DeviceType.NomadE,
);

if (update) {
  console.log("Firmware update available:", update.version);
  console.log("Download:", update.downloadUrl);
}
```

### Compare versions

```ts
release.isVersionNewer("1.1.0", "1.0.0"); // true
release.isVersionNewer("1.0.0", "1.0.0"); // false
release.isVersionNewer("invalid", "1.0.0"); // undefined
```

### Utility helpers

```ts
release.isBeta("1.0.0-rc.1");   // true
release.isBeta("1.0.0");         // false

release.isDevVersion("1.0.0-3-gabcdef0"); // true (commit-hash suffix)
release.isDevVersion("1.0.0-dirty");      // true
release.isDevVersion("1.0.0");            // false (clean release)
```

### Available repositories

| `RepositoryType` member | GitHub repository | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `InputApp` | `input-releases` | Desktop application |
| `NomadFirmware` | `nomad-e-fw-releases` | Nomad E keyboard firmware |
| `KnobFirmware` | `knob-fw-releases` | Knob module firmware |
| `CMicroV2Firmware` | `cm-v2-fw-releases` | Creator Micro V2 firmware |
| `XyzR2Firmware` | `xyz-wb-r2-fw-releases` | XYZ keyboard firmware |

> **Browser renderer:** The `ReleaseInfo` type is available from the browser-safe entrypoint for use in renderer contexts:
> ```ts
> import type { ReleaseInfo } from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit/browser_safe";
> ```

## Firmware flash

Flash firmware to ESP32-based Work Louder devices over serial. The device must be in bootloader (DFU) mode — either by holding the boot button during power-on or via `WLRPCApi.sendIntoBootloader()`. Uses [esptool-js](https://github.com/nicholasgasior/esptool-js) with a Node.js Web Serial polyfill.

### Full workflow (running device → bootloader → flash)

```ts
import {
  WLDeviceDiscovery,
  WLDeviceCommImpl,
  WLRPCApi,
  WLDeviceProgrammer,
} from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit";

const discovery = new WLDeviceDiscovery();
const comm = new WLDeviceCommImpl();

// 1. Connect and reboot into bootloader
const [device] = discovery.findWLDevices();
await comm.connect(device);

const api = new WLRPCApi(comm);
await api.sendIntoBootloader();

// 2. Wait for bootloader to enumerate on serial
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 3000));
const bootloaders = await discovery.findWLBootloaderDevices();

// 3. Flash
const programmer = new WLDeviceProgrammer({
  onProgress(fileIndex, written, total) {
    console.log(`File ${fileIndex + 1}: ${((written / total) * 100).toFixed(1)}%`);
  },
  logger: console,
});

const success = await programmer.flashDeviceFirmware(bootloaders[0], "firmware.bin");
console.log(success ? "Flash complete" : "Flash failed");
```

### Flash only (device already in bootloader)

```ts
import { WLDeviceDiscovery, WLDeviceProgrammer } from "@worklouder/wl-device-kit";

const discovery = new WLDeviceDiscovery();
const bootloaders = await discovery.findWLBootloaderDevices();

const programmer = new WLDeviceProgrammer({
  onProgress(fileIndex, written, total) {
    console.log(`File ${fileIndex + 1}: ${((written / total) * 100).toFixed(1)}%`);
  },
  logger: console,
});

const success = await programmer.flashDeviceFirmware(bootloaders[0], "firmware.bin");
console.log(success ? "Flash complete" : "Flash failed");
```

### `WLDeviceProgrammer` options

| Option | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `onProgress` | `(fileIndex, written, total) => void` | Called repeatedly during flash with byte-level progress |
| `onWriteData` | `(data: string) => void` | Raw serial write data from esptool-js |
| `onWriteLine` | `(data: string) => void` | Line-buffered serial output from esptool-js |
| `clean` | `() => void` | Called when esptool-js clears terminal output |
| `logger` | `Logger` | Optional logger (same interface as other modules) |

> Default baud rate is **921 600**. The device resets automatically after a successful flash. On macOS, grant the terminal app access to serial ports under System Settings → Privacy & Security.

## Custom logger

All constructors accept an optional `Logger` object. Logging is silently disabled when omitted. Pass `console` or a custom logger to enable output:

```ts
const logger = {
  info: (...args: any[]) => myLogger.info(...args),
  error: (...args: any[]) => myLogger.error(...args),
  debug: (...args: any[]) => myLogger.debug(...args),
  warn: (...args: any[]) => myLogger.warn(...args),
};

const discovery = new WLDeviceDiscovery(logger);
const comm = new WLDeviceCommImpl(logger);
const api = new WLRPCApi(comm, logger);
```
